tests.title: A missing or unacceptable credential is refused 401 with one message
given: a protected route with a recording handler
a live API key, a revoked key, an expired key and an unknown string
tests.when: the route is requested with no header, an empty Bearer, a malformed string, the unknown string, the revoked key and the expired key
then: each answers 401 with message "authentication required"
no message says which condition applied
the handler is not invoked for any of them
tests.pseudocode: in the authentication middleware's test file, table over the six credentials: r = get(app, '/api/v1/protected', cred); assert r.status == 401 and r.json.error.message == 'authentication required' and handler.calls == 0

tests.title: An accepted credential is identified by kind, with its user where it has one
given: a live API key, a live PAT and the deployment's admin token
a route that records the identity it was given
tests.when: the route is requested with each credential
then: the API key yields kind api_key and the owning user id
the PAT yields kind pat and the owning user id
the admin token yields kind admin_token and no user id
tests.pseudocode: in the authentication middleware's test file, table over the three credentials: get(app, '/api/v1/whoami', cred); assert recorded.kind == expectedKind and recorded.userId == expectedUser

tests.title: A blocked user's credential stops working without being revoked, and works again after unblocking
given: a user holding a live API key and a live PAT, against the real store
tests.when: the user is blocked, both credentials are used, the user is unblocked, and both are used again
then: both are refused 401 while the user is blocked
neither credential's revoked_at was set
both are accepted again after the unblock
tests.pseudocode: in the authentication integration test file: block(user); assert call(key).status == 401 and call(pat).status == 401; assert store.key(key).revoked_at is None; unblock(user); assert call(key).status == 200

tests.title: No credential secret reaches a log record or a response body
given: a recording log sink
a credential with a distinctive secret portion
tests.when: a successful request, a refused request and a request that raises an unhandled failure are made with that credential
then: no log record contains the credential string or its secret portion
no response body contains either
the log records do contain the request's method and route template, so the scrubbing is of the secret and not of logging generally
tests.pseudocode: in the authentication middleware's test file: for scenario in [ok, refused, boom]: run(scenario, cred='af_k1_SENTINEL9f3a'); assert 'SENTINEL9f3a' not in sink.text and 'SENTINEL9f3a' not in body

tests.title: The public routes are served without a credential
given: a service with the default configuration
tests.when: the four server routes, GET /api/v1/auth/providers, POST /api/v1/auth/callback and the webhook ingress path are requested with no Authorization header
then: none answers 401
each answers the status its own route defines
tests.pseudocode: in the authentication middleware's test file, table over the public routes: assert request(route, noAuth).status != 401

tests.title: API keys and admin tokens hold every scope, and write implies read but not the reverse
given: an API key, an admin token, a PAT holding only workspaces:write and a PAT holding only workspaces:read
tests.when: a route needing workspaces:read and a route needing workspaces:write are called with each credential
then: the API key and the admin token are admitted to both routes
the write-only PAT is admitted to both routes
the read-only PAT is admitted to the read route and refused the write route
tests.pseudocode: in the scope checker's test file, table over (credential, routeScope, expectAdmitted)

tests.title: A PAT without the route's scope is refused 403 with no error_type
given: a PAT holding a scope unrelated to the route under test
tests.when: routes needing each of several different scopes are called with it
then: each answers 403
no body carries an error_type key
the route handler is not invoked
tests.pseudocode: in the scope checker's test file: r = call(route, pat); assert r.status == 403 and 'error_type' not in r.json.error and handler.calls == 0

tests.title: The scope registry accepts exactly the registered names and refuses the retired ones
given: the scope registry
tests.when: a token is created naming each of the 24 hub scopes, each of apikit's 8, each of the eight retired names, and an invented name
then: every registered name is accepted
each retired name is refused 400 with the name in the message
the invented name is refused 400
no token is created for any refused request
tests.pseudocode: in the scope registry's test file, table over the name sets: r = create_token(perms=[name]); assert accepted ? r.status == 201 : (r.status == 400 and name in r.json.error.message)

tests.title: The provider list is public and publicly cacheable
given: a service configured with one OAuth provider
tests.when: GET /api/v1/auth/providers is requested with no credential
then: the response is 200 with an array of {name, authorize_url}
the Cache-Control header permits public caching for 300 seconds
the authorize URL carries the configured client id
tests.pseudocode: in the auth routes' test file: r = get(app, '/api/v1/auth/providers'); assert r.status == 200 and r.json[0].name == 'github' and 'public' in r.headers['Cache-Control']

tests.title: The callback issues a key, revokes the user's older keys and gives a new user a personal organization
given: a stub OAuth provider that accepts one code
a user who already holds two live API keys, and a provider identity belonging to no user
tests.when: the callback is posted for the existing user, and then for the unknown identity
then: each call answers 200 with a user and an api_key whose key matches af_<key_id>_<secret>
both of the existing user's earlier keys are refused 401 afterwards and the new one is accepted
the new user has exactly one organization, owned by them
no other route returns the key string
tests.pseudocode: in the auth routes' integration test file: r = post('/api/v1/auth/callback', {provider, code}); assert matches(r.json.api_key.key, r'^af_[^_]+_.+$'); for old in olds: assert call(old).status == 401; assert len(get('/api/v1/user/orgs', newKey).json) == 1

tests.title: A refused sign-in creates no user, issues no key and revokes none
given: a stub provider, a blocked user, an existing conflicting identity and a redirect allowlist
tests.when: the callback is posted with an invalid code, an expired code, a redirect_uri outside the allowlist, the blocked user's identity, and the conflicting identity
then: the statuses are 401, 401, 400, 403 and 409 respectively
the user table is unchanged after every call
no key is issued and no existing key is revoked
tests.pseudocode: in the auth routes' integration test file, table over the five cases: before = snapshot(); r = post(callback, case); assert r.status == expected and snapshot() == before

tests.title: The key lifetime accepts only 0, 30, 60 and 90 days
given: a stub provider and a fixed clock
tests.when: the callback is posted with expires of 0, 30, 60, 90, omitted, 45, -1 and a non-integer
then: 0 yields a key with a null expires_at
30, 60 and 90 yield expires_at that many days after now
an omitted value behaves as 90
45, -1 and the non-integer are refused 400 and issue no key
tests.pseudocode: in the auth routes' test file, table over the expires values, asserting expires_at against the fixed clock

tests.title: The profile is read, its display name changed, and a bad update refused
given: a user with a profile
tests.when: the profile is read, updated with a full_name, and then updated with no full_name, a null full_name and a body that is not an object
then: the read answers 200 with the ten documented fields
the update answers 200 and only full_name changed
each bad update answers 400 and the stored profile is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the user routes' test file: assert set(get('/api/v1/user').json) == DOCUMENTED_FIELDS; patch(full_name='X'); assert get().json.full_name == 'X' and other fields unchanged; table over bad bodies asserting 400

tests.title: Keys are listed as metadata and a matching ETag answers 304
given: a user holding one live key, one revoked key and one expired key
tests.when: the key list is requested, and then requested again with the returned ETag
then: the first answers 200 with one entry per key carrying key_id, created_at, expires_at and revoked_at
no entry carries a secret or a hash
the second answers 304 with no body
tests.pseudocode: in the key routes' integration test file: r = get('/api/v1/user/keys'); assert all(set(e) == {'key_id','created_at','expires_at','revoked_at'} for e in r.json); r2 = get(headers={'If-None-Match': r.headers['ETag']}); assert r2.status == 304

tests.title: Refreshing a key rotates its secret under the same identifier
given: a user holding one live API key, and a fixed clock
tests.when: the refresh route is called with that key
then: the response is 200 with key, key_id and expires_at
key_id is unchanged and expires_at is recomputed from the key's lifetime
the previous secret is refused 401 and the new one is accepted
tests.pseudocode: in the key routes' integration test file: r = post(f'/api/v1/user/keys/{kid}/refresh', key=old); assert r.json.key_id == kid and r.json.key != old; assert call(old).status == 401 and call(r.json.key).status == 200

tests.title: A key refresh is refused for a PAT caller, a dead key and another user's key
given: a PAT, a revoked key, an expired key and a key belonging to another user
tests.when: the refresh route is called in each of those four ways
then: the PAT caller is refused 401
the revoked and expired keys are refused 400
another user's key is refused 404
no secret is rotated in any case
tests.pseudocode: in the key routes' test file, table over the four cases, asserting the status and that the stored secret hash is unchanged

tests.title: A key is revoked, including the key the request is made with
given: a user holding two live API keys
tests.when: one key is revoked with the other, and then the remaining key is used to revoke itself
then: each revoke answers 204
the self-revoking request completes rather than failing part way
both keys are refused 401 afterwards
tests.pseudocode: in the key routes' integration test file: assert delete(f'/keys/{a}', key=b).status == 204; assert delete(f'/keys/{b}', key=b).status == 204; assert call(a).status == 401 and call(b).status == 401

tests.title: An unknown key and another user's key are indistinguishable
given: a key belonging to another user and an identifier belonging to no key
tests.when: the read and delete key routes are called for each
then: every call answers 404
the two cases produce the same status and the same message
tests.pseudocode: in the key routes' test file: assert resp(foreign).status == resp(missing).status == 404 and resp(foreign).json == resp(missing).json

tests.title: Tokens are listed with their permissions and no secret
given: a user holding two tokens with different permission sets
tests.when: the token list is requested
then: the response is 200 with one entry per token
each entry carries token_id, name, permissions, expires_at, created_at and revoked_at
no entry carries a token string or a hash
tests.pseudocode: in the token routes' test file: r = get('/api/v1/user/tokens'); assert all('token' not in e and 'hash' not in e for e in r.json)

tests.title: A created token is returned once and authenticates on its scopes
given: a user with an API key
tests.when: a token is created with a name, one scope and expires 30, and the token list and token read routes are then called
then: the create answers 201 with a token matching af_pat_<token_id>_<secret>
the token is accepted on a route needing its scope
neither the list nor the read route returns the token string
tests.pseudocode: in the token routes' integration test file: r = post('/api/v1/user/tokens', body); assert matches(r.json.token, r'^af_pat_[^_]+_.+$'); assert call(scopedRoute, r.json.token).status == 200; assert 'token' not in get(f'/api/v1/user/tokens/{tid}').json

tests.title: A PAT cannot grant a scope it does not hold, while an API key can
given: a PAT holding workspaces:read and tokens:manage, and an API key
tests.when: each is used to create a token granting workspaces:write
then: the PAT's request is refused 403 and creates no token
the API key's request succeeds
a PAT granting only scopes it holds succeeds
tests.pseudocode: in the token routes' test file, table over (caller, requestedScopes, expected)

tests.title: Revoking a token answers with its metadata and stops it working
given: a user holding one live token
tests.when: the token is revoked and then used
then: the revoke answers 200, not 204, with the token's metadata and revoked_at set
the token is refused 401 on its next use
tests.pseudocode: in the token routes' integration test file: r = delete(f'/api/v1/user/tokens/{tid}'); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.revoked_at is not None; assert call(token).status == 401

tests.title: Malformed token requests and dead or foreign tokens are refused
given: a live token, a revoked token and a token of another user
tests.when: tokens are created with no name, an over-long name, an empty permission list, a malformed permission list and a bad expires, and the revoked and foreign tokens are revoked
then: each malformed create answers 400 and creates nothing
revoking the already-revoked token answers 400
the foreign token answers 404
tests.pseudocode: in the token routes' test file, two tables: bad create bodies asserting 400 and no row written; revoke cases asserting 400 and 404

tests.title: The three permission verbs replace, add and remove
given: a token holding workspaces:read and patches:read
tests.when: PUT sets [merges:read], PATCH adds [patches:write], DELETE removes [patches:read], and DELETE removes a scope the token does not hold
then: each answers 200 with the token's metadata after the change
the resulting sets are the replacement, the union and the difference respectively
removing an absent scope leaves the set unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the token permission routes' test file, a sequence of calls asserting the permission set after each

tests.title: Replacing a token's permissions with an empty list revokes it
given: a live token holding two scopes
tests.when: PUT is called on its permissions with an empty array, and the token is then used
then: the response is 200 with an empty permissions list and revoked_at set
the token is refused 401 on its next use
tests.pseudocode: in the token permission routes' integration test file: r = put(perms, []); assert r.json.permissions == [] and r.json.revoked_at is not None; assert call(token).status == 401

tests.title: Empty, absent and revoked-token permission changes are refused
given: a live token and a revoked token
tests.when: PATCH and DELETE are called with an empty array, all three verbs are called with permissions absent and with permissions null, and all three are called on the revoked token
then: each answers 400
the live token's permission set and revoked_at are unchanged after every call
tests.pseudocode: in the token permission routes' test file, table over (verb, body, token) asserting 400 and an unchanged stored set

tests.title: A user's organizations are listed, the personal one among them
given: a user with a personal organization who is also a member of one other
tests.when: GET /api/v1/user/orgs is requested
then: the response is 200 with both organizations
each carries id, name, slug, url, owner_id, status, created_at and updated_at
tests.pseudocode: in the org routes' integration test file: r = get('/api/v1/user/orgs'); assert {o.slug for o in r.json} == {personal.slug, other.slug}

tests.title: An organization is read by id with ETag support
given: an organization the caller is a member of, and an admin credential
tests.when: GET /api/v1/orgs/:id is requested by the member and by the admin, then repeated with the returned ETag
then: both callers get 200 with the organization
the repeat with a matching ETag answers 304 with no body
tests.pseudocode: in the org routes' integration test file: r = get(f'/api/v1/orgs/{oid}'); assert r.status == 200; assert get(f'/api/v1/orgs/{oid}', ifNoneMatch=r.headers['ETag']).status == 304

tests.title: A non-member is refused an organization and an unknown id is not found
given: an organization the caller does not belong to, and an id belonging to no organization
tests.when: GET /api/v1/orgs/:id is requested for each
then: the non-member case answers 403
the unknown id answers 404
tests.pseudocode: in the org routes' test file: assert get(other).status == 403 and get(missing).status == 404

tests.title: Administration routes admit only an admin token or an admin-role key
given: an admin token, an API key of an admin-role user, an API key of an ordinary user, and a PAT holding every registered scope
tests.when: a representative route from each administration family is called with each credential, and once with no credential
then: the admin token and the admin-role key are admitted
the ordinary key and the all-scope PAT are refused 403
the credential-less request is refused 401
tests.pseudocode: in the admin routes' test file, table over (route, credential, expected)

tests.title: An administrator manages users through their whole lifecycle
given: an admin credential and an empty user table beyond the admin
tests.when: a user is created, listed, read, read again with the returned ETag, updated and deleted, and a second create repeats the username
then: the create answers 201 and the duplicate answers 409
list and read answer 200, and the conditional read answers 304
the update answers 200 with the new full_name and the delete answers 204
the deleted user no longer appears in the list
tests.pseudocode: in the admin routes' integration test file, a sequence over POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/users

tests.title: Promote, demote, block and unblock take effect and repeat safely
given: an admin credential, a second admin, and an ordinary user holding a live key
tests.when: the ordinary user is promoted, promoted again, demoted, blocked and then unblocked, with their key used after the block and after the unblock
then: each call answers 200 and the second promote changes nothing
the user's role reflects each change
the key is refused 401 while blocked and accepted after the unblock
tests.pseudocode: in the admin routes' integration test file, a sequence asserting the role and the key's behaviour after each step

tests.title: The last active admin cannot be deleted or demoted
given: a deployment with exactly one active admin, and one with two
tests.when: that admin is demoted and deleted in the one-admin deployment, and one of the two is demoted in the other
then: both calls in the one-admin deployment answer 409 and leave the user an active admin
the demote in the two-admin deployment succeeds
tests.pseudocode: in the admin routes' test file, table over (adminCount, action, expected)

tests.title: An administrator lists and revokes another user's credentials
given: an admin credential and a user holding one API key and one token
tests.when: that user's keys and tokens are listed, and each is revoked, and the user then makes a request with each
then: each list answers 200 with entries carrying user_id and no secret
each revoke answers 204
both credentials are refused 401 afterwards
tests.pseudocode: in the admin routes' integration test file: assert all('user_id' in e for e in list_keys(uid)); delete(key); assert call(key).status == 401

tests.title: An administrator manages organizations through their whole lifecycle
given: an admin credential
tests.when: an organization is created, listed, updated, blocked, unblocked and deleted, and creates are repeated with a duplicate name, a duplicate slug and an invalid slug
then: the create answers 201 and the lifecycle calls answer 200 or 204
the duplicate name and duplicate slug answer 409
the invalid slug answers 400 and creates nothing
tests.pseudocode: in the admin routes' integration test file, a sequence over the organization routes plus a table of refused creates

tests.title: An administrator adds and removes organization members
given: an admin credential, an organization and two users
tests.when: the members are listed, one user is added, the list is read again, that user is removed, and the list is read once more
then: add answers 200 with a membership of org_id, user_id, username, email, role and created_at
the added user appears in the list and the removed user does not
remove answers 204
tests.pseudocode: in the admin routes' integration test file: put(member); assert uid in ids(list_members()); delete(member); assert uid not in ids(list_members())

tests.title: A developer signs in end to end and their previous key stops working
given: a running deployment with an OAuth provider configured against a stub authorization server
a user who already holds a live API key
tests.when: the provider list is fetched, the stub provider issues a code, the code is posted to the callback, and the old key is then used
then: the callback answers 200 with a user and a new API key
the new key authenticates a subsequent request
the previously held key is refused 401
the user has a personal organization
tests.pseudocode: in the identity smoke test file, against a running deployment: providers = get('/api/v1/auth/providers'); code = stub.authorize(); r = post('/api/v1/auth/callback', {provider, code}); assert call(r.json.api_key.key).status == 200 and call(oldKey).status == 401

tests.title: A minted token is admitted on its scope and refused outside it, against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and a signed-in user with an API key
tests.when: a token granting workspaces:read alone is created, then used on a route needing tokens:manage and on a route needing workspaces:read
then: the create answers 201 and returns the token once
the route needing tokens:manage answers 403 with no error_type
the route needing workspaces:read admits the token
tests.pseudocode: in the identity smoke test file: t = post('/api/v1/user/tokens', {name, permissions:['workspaces:read']}).json.token; assert call(tokensManageRoute, t).status == 403; assert call(workspacesReadRoute, t).status != 403

tests.title: Blocking a user stops their live key against a running deployment, and unblocking restores it
given: a running deployment, an administrator credential and a user holding a live API key
tests.when: the user is blocked, the key is used, the user is unblocked, and the key is used again
then: the key is refused 401 while the user is blocked
the key's revoked_at is still null in the administrator's listing
the key is admitted again after the unblock
tests.pseudocode: in the identity smoke test file: post(f'/api/v1/users/{uid}/block', admin); assert call(key).status == 401; assert list_keys(uid, admin)[0].revoked_at is None; post(f'/api/v1/users/{uid}/unblock', admin); assert call(key).status == 200
